structure: Part 9: animals e2e/journeys — what is stored and what is published. Read in full: the 4 specs under tests/animals/e2e/journeys/persistence (persistence-notification.spec.ts, persistence-multi-commodity.spec.ts, persistence-accompanying-document.spec.ts, api-seed-parity.spec.ts), the 3 under tests/animals/e2e/journeys/dynamics (notification-data.spec.ts, notification-data-gaps.spec.ts, notification-events.spec.ts), tests/animals/security/backend/notification-submission.spec.ts, and the models and support the eight rest on: domain/animals/models/db (notification-document.ts, accompanying-document.ts, outbox-event-document.ts), domain/animals/models/api (notification.ts, notification-status.ts, notification-fulfilments.ts), domain/animals/models/dynamics/importer-notification.ts, domain/ins/models/db (aggregated-notification-document.ts, address-document.ts), domain/animals/constants (commodity-lines.ts, journey-commodity-line-answers.ts, document-types.ts, commodity-names.ts, journey-options.ts read as context), every file of adapters/http (rest-client, frontend-form-client, notification-api-client, ins-notification-api-client, address-book-api-client, reference-data-api-client, animals-dynamics-client, dataverse-client, organisation, expect-api-refusal), adapters/db/mongodb-client.ts, adapters/queue/sqs-client.ts, flows/animals/seeded-journey.ts, flows/animals/seed-form-steps.ts, fixtures/seed-context.ts, fixtures/security.ts, bin/seed-notification.ts, utils/dynamics/animals-polls.ts, config/dynamics.ts, config/dataverse.ts and resources/outbox-events (notification-submitted-outbox-event.json, paths.ts). Counted by Bash grep, the eight specs hold 17 test() declarations, not the 57 the partition's covers names (persistence-notification 2 not 6, persistence-multi-commodity 1 not 4, persistence-accompanying-document 1 not 4, api-seed-parity 4 not 10, notification-data 3 not 11, notification-data-gaps 2 not 9, notification-events 3 not 11, backend security 1 not 2); none of them generates tests in a loop, so every declaration is claimed by its title and the count difference is recorded as a gap. Covered: what a notification, its commodity lines and its accompanying documents hold once stored in Mongo; the parity rule the API seed is held to and where the suite lets a seeded and a browser-driven notification differ; what reaches PIMS Dynamics, which columns the suite proves and which it records as empty with test.fixme; the outbox event, aggregated notification and address document shapes the models carry; the notification API wire shape and endpoint surface; and the one backend security test.

claims.statement: Every assertion about what a notification holds once stored runs only against the Docker Compose stack, because that is the only environment whose Mongo the suite can read.
claims.quote: skipUnlessComposeEnvironment('the round-trip asserts on Mongo directly, which only the compose stack exposes');
claims.note: The same beforeEach guard heads all four persistence specs. utils/playwright/environment.ts counts localhost, 127.0.0.1 and cdp-docker.test as the compose stack.

claims.quote: const collection = client.collection<NotificationDocument>('trade-imports-animals-backend', 'notification');

claims.statement: A journey stores exactly one notification document for its reference number.
claims.quote: await expect.poll(() => collection.countDocuments({ referenceNumber }), { timeout: timeouts.short }).toBe(1);

claims.statement: A party on a notification is stored as a copy of the address-book record with no link back to it: the stored party carries no address id.
claims.quote: expect(notification.consignor).not.toHaveProperty('addressId');
claims.note: domain/animals/models/db/notification-document.ts:12-15 states the same: "A copy of the address-book record picked for the role, with no link back to it. An unanswered role has none of these fields, so every field is optional."

claims.statement: A stored party holds the chosen address-book record's name, email and phone, and an address holding address line 1, town or city, postcode and country code.
A stored address holds address line 1, an optional address line 2, town or city, an optional county, postcode and country code.
A notification stores six parties separately: place of destination, consignee, importer, place of origin, consignor, and the consignment contact.
claims.note: The contact address is stored under the key `consignment`.

claims.statement: The names, emails, phones and addresses a notification stores are read back from the address book by name, so the stored party must match the live address-book record.
claims.quote: const consignor = await addressBookApi.findByName(answers.parties.consignor);
claims.note: adapters/http/address-book-api-client.ts:116-122 refuses unless exactly one live address holds the name.

claims.quote: expect(doc.preAmendNotification).toBeUndefined();
claims.note: domain/animals/models/db/notification-document.ts:106 calls it a "Pre-amend snapshot of notification content. Present only during an in-flight amendment."

claims.statement: A notification stores the CPH number as one unbroken string of the county, parish and holding digits, with no separators.
claims.quote: expect(notification.cphNumber).toBe(CPH_NUMBER);

claims.quote: expect(doc.status).toBe(notificationStatuses.submitted);

claims.statement: An accompanying document is stored in its own collection, accompanying_documents, in the animals backend's database, keyed to the notification by its reference number.
claims.quote: const collection = client.collection<AccompanyingDocumentModel>('trade-imports-animals-backend', 'accompanying_documents');

claims.statement: Uploading one document stores exactly one accompanying-document record for the notification.
An accompanying document stores the document reference the trader typed.
claims.quote: expect(doc.documentReference).toBe(documentReference);

claims.statement: An accompanying document stores an upload id in UUID form.
An accompanying document stores its date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD calendar date, converted from the day, month and year the trader typed.
claims.note: The issue date was typed as '03/01/2026'; the stored value drops the leading zeroes before conversion.

claims.statement: An accompanying document's scan status reaches COMPLETE once the virus scan has finished.
claims.quote: await expect.poll(() => collection.findOne({ uploadId: doc.uploadId }).then((d) => d?.scanStatus)).toBe('COMPLETE');

claims.statement: An accompanying document stores its type as the code the select submits, such as ITAHC, not as the label shown to the trader.
claims.quote: expect(doc.documentType).toBe('ITAHC');

claims.statement: An accompanying document stores a files list, each file holding the original filename, the declared content type, the byte length of the file uploaded, an S3 key, the content type detected on scanning and a SHA-256 checksum.
An uploaded file's S3 key begins with the notification's reference number and the upload id, so files are stored under a per-notification, per-upload path.
claims.quote: expect(file.s3Key).toMatch(new RegExp(`^${referenceNumber}/${doc.uploadId}/`));

claims.statement: An accompanying-document record also holds a version, a correlation id, an S3 bucket, a per-file status, and created and updated timestamps.

claims.note: The describe block names the rule: 'Seeded and browser-driven notifications match'.

claims.statement: A seeded notification names the party the answers name, so changing one party's name changes the stored consignor on both the seeded and the browser-driven notification.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/journeys/persistence/api-seed-parity.spec.ts:70 'a seeded notification names the party the answers name, as the browser journey does'
claims.quote:
expect(browserDoc.notification.consignor?.name).toBe(OTHER_CONSIGNOR_NAME);
    expect(seededDoc.notification.consignor?.name).toBe(OTHER_CONSIGNOR_NAME);
claims.note: The other consignor is 'Alpine Dairy GmbH' (api-seed-parity.spec.ts:9).

claims.statement: The parity rule lets a seeded and a browser-driven notification differ on everything outside the notification content, the status and the fulfilments — the reference number, the document id and the created and updated timestamps are never compared.
claims.note: Follows because each test reads two whole documents and asserts only these three members; the stored document also holds _id, referenceNumber, created, updated and _class (notification-document.ts:101-112).

claims.statement: The API seed cannot produce a notification with an accompanying document, because its form client sends no files, so parity is never proven for an uploaded document.

A seeded notification is made by posting the frontend's own save-and-continue forms in journey order: origin, a commodity search per line then the species choice, consignment details, commodity identification, import reason, additional details, the five party selections, the permanent address where a species needs one, the addresses page, the CPH number, the port of entry, the transit countries, the transporter, and the consignment contact.
claims.note: mechanism: turns one set of notification answers into the form fields each page expects, so a seeded notification exercises the same routes the browser does.

claims.statement: A notification is created by posting to the live-animals set's notifications path, and the frontend answers with a redirect to the new notification's origin page carrying its reference number.
claims.quote:
export const CREATE_PATH = `${SET_BASES.liveAnimals}/notifications`;
export const CREATED_AT_ORIGIN = new RegExp(`^${CREATE_PATH}/(?<referenceNumber>[^/?]+)/origin${OPTIONAL_RETURN_AND_TRAIL_PATTERN}$`);

claims.statement: A seeded draft can be left at one of three stages: unlocked (origin and commodity answered, which opens the other tasks), partial (on through arrival) or ready (every section answered, so the draft can be declared).

Declaring a notification takes two posts to the declaration page — one marked as the review step and one marked as the declaration, each carrying a concurrency token read from the page before it — and the second redirects to the confirmation page.
Declaring a draft that is not finished is refused: the post redirects back to the notification view with a refused marker in the query string.
claims.quote: { redirectsTo: /\/notification-view\?refused=1$/ },

claims.statement: Amending, cancelling an amendment and deleting a notification are each a post to the notification's own path, redirecting respectively to the notification view, to the notification view with a cancelled marker, and to a page with a deleted marker.

A notification can be seeded from the command line in a draft, submitted or amend state, optionally answering every optional question bar the accompanying document, and the command prints the new reference number.
claims.quote:
const USAGE = `Usage: npm run --silent seed:notification -- [--state draft|submitted|amend] [--all-answers]

Seeds a notification through the frontend and prints its reference number.

  --state        draft, submitted or amend (default submitted)
  --all-answers  answer every optional question too, bar the accompanying document
                 (default: only the answers the frontend requires)

claims.statement: Every form post to the frontend carries a CSRF crumb minted by loading the set's own dashboard, and no set is served at the root: the root is a server-wide redirect to the default set.
claims.quote:
The page the crumb cookie is minted from. No set is served at the root any
 * more — `/` is a server-wide 302 to the default set — so land on the set's own
 * dashboard.

claims.statement: A submitted notification is published to PIMS Dynamics as one row of the importer notifications table, found by its reference number in the row's name column.
claims.quote:
const NOTIFICATIONS_ENTITY_SET = 'defraimp_importernotifications';
const REFERENCE_COLUMN = 'defraimp_name';

claims.statement: Submitting a notification creates exactly one PIMS Dynamics record for its reference number.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/journeys/dynamics/notification-events.spec.ts:37 'submitting a notification creates one PIMS Dynamics record'
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_name).toBe(referenceNumber);
claims.note: utils/dynamics/animals-polls.ts:35-37 polls until the table holds exactly one row for the reference.

claims.statement: A submitted notification's PIMS Dynamics record shows the status 'Submitted' and version 1.
claims.quote:
expect.soft(formattedValue(row, 'defraimp_status')).toBe('Submitted');
    expect.soft(row.defraimp_version).toBe(1);

claims.statement: A submitted notification's PIMS Dynamics record carries a submission date, set to the backend's own submit time within about ten seconds of it.
claims.quote:
// PIMS Dynamics stores the backend's submit time, slightly before the test's own; the tolerance also covers clock skew.
    const submissionDateToleranceMs = timeouts.medium;
claims.note: timeouts.medium is 10,000 ms (config/timeouts.ts:4).

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics names the signed-in user who submitted it, by display name.
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_submittedbydisplayname, 'submitted by').toBe(defaultUser.displayName);
claims.note: The default signed-in identity is 'Andrew Farmer' (config/users.ts:5-25).

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics names its country of origin by the country's display name, through a lookup rather than a code.
claims.quote: expect.soft(formattedValue(row, '_defraimp_countryoforiginid_value'), 'country of origin').toBe(answers.countryCode.display);

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics says whether the consignment includes unweaned animals as a true or false flag, and a 'no' answer arrives as false.
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_commoditiesincludenonablactedanimals, 'unweaned animals').toBe(false);

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics carries each of the five parties — consignor, place of destination, place of origin, consignee and importer — as a company name, an address line 1, a city and a country lookup.
PIMS Dynamics names countries in full: Switzerland, Ireland, and 'United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland' for GB.
claims.note: mechanism: maps the address book's country code to the label PIMS returns, so the test can compare the two. The labels are PIMS's, not the service's.

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics carries the arrival date, whose date part is the arrival date stored by the service.
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_arrivaldate?.slice(0, 10), 'arrival date').toBe(toIsoDate(parseAppDateText(answers.arrivalDate)));

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics carries the port of entry as its code, not its name.
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_portofentry, 'point of entry').toBe(answers.pointOfEntry.value);

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics names the means of transport to the entry point in PIMS's own words: Aeroplane, Railway Wagon, Road Vehicle or Ship.
claims.note: mechanism: maps the service's means-of-transport code to the label PIMS stores. It also records the service's four codes: AIRPLANE, RAILWAY, ROAD_VEHICLE, VESSEL.

claims.statement: A notification published to PIMS Dynamics names the transporter by company name.
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_transportercompanyname, 'transporter').toBe(answers.transporter.display);

claims.statement: The rest of the transporter published to PIMS Dynamics — approval number, type, address lines 1 and 2 and country — comes from the transporter's reference record rather than the trader's answers, so the suite proves only that each is filled in.
claims.quote:
// The rest of the transporter comes from its reference record, not the answers, so only its presence is asserted.
    expect.soft(row.defraimp_transporterapprovalnumber, 'transporter approval number').not.toBeNull();

claims.statement: When the trader answers only what the journey requires, the region of origin code, the internal reference, the number of packages and the transited countries reach PIMS Dynamics empty, because neither PIMS nor the gateway fills them in by default.
claims.note: The test that proves this is 'a notification submitted with only the mandatory answers is stored in PIMS Dynamics'.

claims.statement: When the trader gives an internal reference, it reaches PIMS Dynamics as the trader reference.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/journeys/dynamics/notification-data.spec.ts:127 'a notification submitted with every answer is stored in PIMS Dynamics with its internal reference'
claims.quote: expect.soft(row.defraimp_traderreference, 'internal reference').toBe(answers.internalReference);

claims.statement: A 'yes' answer to unweaned animals does not reach PIMS Dynamics: the record is not written from the message the service publishes.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/journeys/dynamics/notification-data.spec.ts:115-116 'answering yes to unweaned animals is stored in PIMS Dynamics'
claims.quote: test.fixme(true, 'PIMS Dynamics does not yet write isOrHasUnweanedAnimals from the 0.1.0 message to the record');
claims.note: The test is written and marked fixme, so the behaviour is specified but not proven.

claims.statement: A long list of answers the journey requires does not reach PIMS Dynamics at all: the contact address, the species Latin and common names, every party's postcode, phone and email, the CPH number, the transport document reference, the reason for import, the internal market purpose, what the animals are certified for, the number of animals, the ear tag and the transport identification are all left empty.
claims.quote: test.fixme(true, 'PIMS Dynamics leaves these mandatory answers empty; the likely cause of each is in the comments');
claims.note: The test's own title names every one of them. It is marked fixme, so none is proven today.

claims.statement: Four optional answers do not reach PIMS Dynamics either: the region of origin code, the transited countries, the number of packages and the passport number.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/journeys/dynamics/notification-data-gaps.spec.ts:92-97 'the region of origin code, transited countries, number of packages and passport number are stored in PIMS Dynamics'
claims.quote: test.fixme(true, 'PIMS Dynamics leaves these optional answers empty; the likely cause of each is in the comments');

claims.statement: Each field the suite expects PIMS Dynamics to hold is traced to the place in the published notification document it should come from, and to the message version that added it: v0.3.0 for the issuer's postal address and the region of origin code, v0.2.0 for the species names, each party's postcode, phone and email and the transit countries, and v0.1.0 for the clauses carrying the purpose, internal market purpose and certification.
claims.note: The markers 'OPTION NOT MATCHED?' and 'NOT MAPPED?' record the suite's own reading of why each field is empty: either the option set does not match the value sent, or the field is not mapped at all.

claims.statement: The animal identifiers published to PIMS Dynamics are expected in one free-text identification column, with the ear tag and the passport number each appearing within it rather than in fields of their own.
The contact address is expected to reach PIMS Dynamics as one free-text block holding the address line, the town and the postcode together.

claims.statement: A submission event is published under the event type NotificationSubmitted, with a schema version and a schema URL under schemas.defra.gov.uk naming the event and its version.

An outbox event can carry the actor who caused it — an id, a source, a user type, a display name, an organisation id and an organisation acted on behalf of — and a list of status changes, each a status, the date it changed and the actor who changed it.
The notification published to other services is a GBN-AG document with two halves: an exchanged document and a specified consignment.

The published exchanged document carries the notification's identifier, the trader's own assigned id, a notification status code, a version id, an issue date and time, the issuer, a list of signed clauses, and a list of referenced documents.

The published specified consignment carries the consignor, consignee, despatch, delivery, importer and carrier parties, the origin country, the unloading base port, the final destination, the main carriage transport movements, the transit countries, whether the consignment holds unweaned animals, and the consignment items.

A published trade line item carries a description, the scientific and common species names, a product unit quantity per delivery, an item quantity per package, and the individual animals, each with a name and a list of identifiers.
Each animal identifier is published as a type code and a content value, so the kind of identifier (ear tag, passport and so on) travels as a code beside the number.
claims.note: notification-data-gaps.spec.ts:86 and :120 name EAR_TAG and PASSPORT as two of those type codes.

claims.statement: A published party carries an identifier, a URL id, a name, a party role code and a list of party type codes, each coded value being a value with an optional URL id and name.

A published country carries a code, its subordinate country sub-divisions and a region of origin code; a published location carries an identifier, a URL id, a name and a type code; and a published transport movement carries a numeric mode code and the transport contract documents.

The canned submission event the suite keeps carries a flat summary of the notification — reference number, status, point of entry and a commodities list of species name and number of animals — not the GBN-AG document the outbox event model describes.
claims.note: An ambiguity recorded, not settled: outbox-event-document.ts:9 types `data` as GbnAgEventData, and the canned file also carries an eventId and a publishedAt that the model does not. The reconciler should decide which shape is current.

claims.statement: The INS read model holds one aggregated notification per notification, carrying an aggregate version, the organisation id, the reference number, the status, the origin country, a single commodity, the arrival date and when it was last updated.

claims.statement: The notification API also carries a concurrency token, the created and updated times, and the time the notification was submitted.
A notification's fulfilments are stored as entries against an obligation: either one value for the obligation, or a list of records each with its own fulfilment id and value.

A notification's fulfilments can be read on their own, returning the reference number, the current fulfilments, the fulfilments as they were at submission, the status, when it was created and when it was submitted.

The notification API offers creating a notification, replacing it whole, submitting it, amending it, cancelling an amendment, copying it, soft-deleting it, counting notifications by reference number, and reading its fulfilments.
claims.quote: /** PUT /notifications/{id} — whole-record replace; optional actor metadata. */
claims.note: Submit and copy take the concurrency token as a query parameter; create and save take optional actor metadata in the body.
